---
title: "env"
sidebarTitle: "Overview"
description: "Import, update, and synchronize the Gateway-owned environment configuration of one Instance."
covers:
  - apps/cli/app/Commands/Environment/**
---

The Gateway stores the environment configuration of every Instance as encrypted keys and values. The `env` family imports an existing `.env`, changes one stored value, and writes the complete stored configuration back into the Instance's `.env`. Import and sync run as Swamp Operations that the CLI follows to the end; update changes stored configuration at once.

[Instance environment variables](/reference/environment-variables) describes the file location, the limits, the placeholders, and the error codes.

## Commands

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| [`env:import`](/cli/env/import) | Import the Instance's `.env` into stored configuration. |
| [`env:update`](/cli/env/update) | Add or replace one stored value. |
| [`env:sync`](/cli/env/sync) | Replace the Instance's `.env` with the complete stored configuration, after checking the key names the Node agent reports. |

Every command takes `--instance=SELECTOR`: a positive Instance ID or the exact domain of its Route. An omitted or empty selector returns `env.instance_required` before the CLI sends a request. The Instance must have exactly one Route; otherwise the Gateway returns `env.owner_unavailable`. Every command accepts `--json`. Import and update output holds the Instance ID, the operation, whether something changed, the total stored key count, and the request ID. `env:sync` starts an [operation](/reference/operations) and follows it, as described below. Values never appear. Import and update change stored configuration only; the file stays the same until you run `env:sync`. On a container Instance that sync writes only the connection keys and the keys `env:update` stored since the last sync. A changed production sync also rebuilds an existing release config cache and refreshes FPM's opcache; `env:update` alone does neither.

## Related

- [`instance:database:add`](/cli/instance/database-add) writes database keys into the same stored configuration.
- [`instance:deploy`](/cli/instance/deploy) synchronizes the stored configuration before it runs deploy steps.
- [`doctor`](/cli/doctor) reports when a production `.env` differs from the stored configuration.
